text:
Pavel Zacha's name has been everywhere in the last week, and not for anything he did on the ice. Yahoo Sports linked him to the Dylan Larkin talks before Larkin went to Montreal, and the same outlet carried an insider saying an extension with Boston looks unlikely. A 29-year-old center in a contract year, on a team deciding what it is, is going to hear his name a lot.

The hockey is steady. He has 17 points in 22 games, eight on the power play, at about 19 minutes a night, and his nine points in the last ten games match what his chances and ice time say he should have. The one soft spot: Boston has been out-shot with him at five on five (47% of attempts) and is 3.2 points of expected-goal share worse with him than without, while scoring 5 goals more than its chances deserve when he's out there.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 60% of his entries last season and getting to the home-plate area at an 86th percentile rate. Watch the trade wire as much as the box score.
